summary: Eagle Ambulance, of San Leandro, will provide ride-along experiences for district students enrolled in the Highway to Work: Emergency Medical Technician program. There is no cost to the district. The agreement covers July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, so it started before this ratification vote.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Robert Half, Inc. - General Counsel
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-27 by and between the District and Robert Half, Inc., Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide contract talent solutions to the District, via the Legal Department, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for the period of July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $119,000.00.
headline: Pays Robert Half up to $119,000.00 for contract talent services for the Legal Department
summary: Robert Half, Inc., of Oakland, will provide contract talent services to the district's Legal Department, as described in the agreement. The cost is capped at $119,000.00 for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. The start date is before this ratification vote.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding and Engagement Policy - Olson Remcho Law Firm - General Counsel
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding and Engagement Policy by and between the District and Olson Remcho Law Firm, authorizing the Office of the General Counsel to retain Olson Remcho Law Firm to provide legal services to the District for advice and counsel relating to the Oakland Unified School District Teacher Retention and Educational Programs Replacement Act; and to provide additional legal services related to elections, campaign finance, ethics, constitutional, government, public policy law, and litigation defense, on an as needed basis, for the period of  July 20, 2026 through June 30, 2028, in an amount not to exceed $114,000 in a fiscal year.
headline: Retains Olson Remcho Law Firm for up to $114,000 a year in legal advice through June 2028
summary: The district's General Counsel may use Olson Remcho Law Firm for advice on the Teacher Retention and Educational Programs Replacement Act. The firm may also help with elections, campaign finance, ethics, constitutional and public policy law, and litigation defense, as needed. Fees are capped at $114,000 in a fiscal year for July 20, 2026 to June 30, 2028, and the start date is before this ratification vote.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement - LogicTree IT Solutions, Inc. = Risk Management Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Service Agreement by and between the District and LogicTree IT Solutions, Inc, Citrus Heights, CA, for the latter to provide “a FormsTrackR subscription configured for the current Tips Management features currently used with the District’s HubConnect system through LogicTree IT Solutions Inc. Include additional features to add 30 additional sites and required “associates” which are staff that have access to receive and manage incoming tips including assigning tips to responding staff. Convert the current HubConnect platform features and system data to the new FormsTrackR management system through LogicTree IT Solutions Inc.” for the term July 16, 2026 through June 30, 2029, in an amount not to exceed $45,425.50, via Risk Management Department.
funding_source: Learning Communities for School Success Program (LCSSP) - Prop 47, Cohort 7 Grant
headline: Pays LogicTree up to $45,425.50 for a new tip-management system through June 2029
summary: LogicTree IT Solutions, of Citrus Heights, will provide a FormsTrackR subscription for managing incoming tips, adding 30 more sites and staff accounts to receive and assign tips. It will also move the district's current HubConnect tips features and data into the new system. The cost is capped at $45,425.50 for July 16, 2026 to June 30, 2029, and the start date is before this ratification vote.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Facilities Committee – August 20, 2026 - Valarie Bachelor, Chairperson

official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education, of Resolution No. 2627-0101 Authorizing the Demolition of Obsolete Portable Buildings and Site Stabilization at the Former John Swett Elementary and Tilden Child Development Center Campus in Support of the Facilities Master Plan and District Asset Management Strategy.
headline: Adopts a resolution to demolish obsolete portable buildings at the former John Swett and Tilden campus
summary: This resolution authorizes demolishing obsolete portable buildings and stabilizing the site at the former John Swett Elementary and Tilden Child Development Center campus. schools: Former John Swett Elementary; Tilden Child Development Center

title: Services Agreement - Eve Gordon - Board of Education
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement by and between the District and Eve Gordon, Alameda, CA, for the latter to provide facilitation, leadership development, and governance support services to the Board of Education for the period of June 1, 2026, through February 1, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $15,600.00.

group: Measure G1 - Districtwide Teacher Retention and Middle School Improvement Act Oversight Commission – August 11, 2026, Chairperson, Frederick Mesa
title: Measure G1 Districtwide Teacher Retention and Middle School Improvement Act Oversight Commission - 2026-2027 School Year Amended Measure G1 Funding Application - Named Schools
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2627-0151 - Measure G1 - Districtwide Teacher Retention and Middle School Improvement Act Oversight Commission Recommendation Approving 2026-2027 School Year Amended G1 Applications for Named Schools.
headline: Approves amended 2026-27 Measure G1 funding applications for named schools
summary: The Board is asked to adopt a resolution accepting the recommendation of the Measure G1 oversight commission. The commission reviews how schools use Measure G1 money, which supports teacher retention and middle school improvement. The resolution approves amended 2026-2027 school year funding applications for the schools named in it. The text does not state dollar amounts.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Measure G1 - Districtwide Teacher Retention and Middle School Improvement Act Oversight Commission – August 11, 2026, Chairperson, Frederick Mesa
title: Measure G1 - Districtwide Teacher Retention and Middle School Improvement Act Oversight Commission – Carryover Allocation for Named Schools – School Year 2025 – 2026
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2627-0153 Measure G1 - Districtwide Teacher Retention and Middle School Improvement Act Oversight Commission Recommendation - Approving 2025-2026 Carryover Allocation for Named School, in the culminative amount of $1,372,113.00.
headline: Approves $1,372,113 in 2025-26 Measure G1 carryover funds for named schools
summary: The Board is asked to adopt a resolution accepting the Measure G1 oversight commission's recommendation. It approves carrying over unspent 2025-2026 Measure G1 money, totaling $1,372,113, to the schools named in the resolution. Measure G1 supports teacher retention and middle school improvement.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
